meta.title: Supabase × KINGDOM
meta.note: A source-linked design map, not a deployment inventory. Layer connections are proposed fits within KINGDOM’s seven existing layers. Every composition is an experiment; opening this file makes no provider request.

layers.label: Soul
layers.summary: Preserve the meaning and provenance of declarations. Storage and search do not certify practice, consent, or rights.

layers.label: Runtime
layers.summary: Support explicitly authorized, finite execution with delivery records, budgets, and stop conditions.

layers.label: Nervous
layers.summary: Connect discovery, correspondence, notifications, and durable cursors. AgentTool declares this layer.

layers.label: Fleet
layers.summary: Rehearse releases, restores, and regional public reads. Deployment stays with the existing operator path.

layers.label: Economy
layers.summary: Keep exact units and immutable ledger transitions. Transport acknowledgments cannot establish settlement.

layers.label: Commerce
layers.summary: Explore participant-owned services and scoped application identity without creating a second payment lifecycle.

layers.label: OS
layers.summary: Offer an intelligible catalog and offline Commons. Keep provider operations outside the accountless reader.

capabilities.label: Postgres + scoped roles
capabilities.summary: Relational state, transactions, constraints, and explicit application permissions form the base for rebuildable projections.
capabilities.caveat: The inventory role bypasses RLS. It is not a suitable proof of tenant isolation or a model for an application role.

capabilities.label: SQL hybrid search
capabilities.summary: Combine full-text matching and vector similarity while returning exact source revision and digest references.
capabilities.caveat: Embeddings and ranking SQL need implementation. A high similarity score is not evidence of truth or current authority.

capabilities.label: Structured declaration checks
capabilities.summary: Apply JSON Schema constraints to a derived JSON/JSONB projection of cards and evidence metadata.
capabilities.caveat: Structural validity does not check signatures or semantics. Preserve exact canonical bytes outside any JSONB reserialization.

capabilities.label: Durable queues
capabilities.summary: Keep finite work delivery near application records in PostgreSQL. Use idempotent effects and explicit retry bounds.
capabilities.caveat: Matching upstream SQL uses INSERT and row locks with visibility leases. This does not guarantee exactly-once external effects or authorize execution.

capabilities.label: Cron
capabilities.summary: Schedule bounded dispatch and reconciliation, with a record of scheduled runs.
capabilities.status: pg_cron 1.6.4 installed; five active jobs observed 2026-09-05
capabilities.caveat: A completed scheduled run is not proof that a remote effect completed. Existing schedules were inventoried, not changed.

capabilities.label: Post-commit HTTP
capabilities.summary: Use pg_net for asynchronous transport after the surrounding database transaction commits.
capabilities.caveat: Version 0.20.0 creates private request and response tables as UNLOGGED. Keep durable intent elsewhere. The POST path serializes JSONB rather than guaranteeing original input bytes; retain signed bytes separately or in an explicit encoding.

capabilities.label: Vault
capabilities.summary: Resolve selected database-side secrets at a narrow dispatch boundary.
capabilities.caveat: Vault has a decrypted view for authorized SQL access. It is not client-side encryption or a replacement for the caller’s signing-key custody.

capabilities.label: Realtime hints + replay
capabilities.summary: Private channels can carry minimal record IDs so returning clients know where to reconcile history.
capabilities.caveat: Replay covers database-origin private messages and at most 25 messages. Channel authorization is cached until subscription or JWT refresh; policy changes alone do not promise immediate existing-channel revocation. Reconcile durable history separately.

capabilities.label: S3-compatible object storage
capabilities.summary: Store application-encrypted artifacts through the existing ADDS object-plane boundary.
capabilities.status: Storage catalog observed; proposed encrypted bucket not provisioned
capabilities.caveat: Database backups omit object bytes. Standard S3 compatibility lacks versioning and Object Lock; storage acknowledgment alone is not recovery proof.

capabilities.label: Local development + branches
capabilities.summary: Use synthetic environments to rehearse schema, role, function, and object recovery behavior.
capabilities.caveat: Branches start without production data by default but carry configuration and functions. Merge automation can deploy changes; preserve the canonical migration owner.

capabilities.label: Regional read replicas
capabilities.summary: Serve public declarations with visible revision and freshness from asynchronous regional copies.
capabilities.caveat: This is not global multiwriter support. Auth, Storage, and Realtime do not gain regional execution from a database replica endpoint.

capabilities.label: Edge Functions
capabilities.summary: Run short adapters and dispatch boundaries with explicit application scopes.
capabilities.caveat: Current hosted limits include 256 MB memory and two CPU seconds per request. Long agent sessions need a separately bounded runtime.

capabilities.label: Foreign-data wrappers
capabilities.summary: Expose selected external data as SQL tables for controlled metadata ingestion.
capabilities.caveat: Foreign tables lack RLS. Queries may contact providers; preserve method, scope, pagination, and volume bounds at the adapter.

capabilities.label: OpenAPI through SQL
capabilities.summary: Investigate a generic metadata adapter with schema import and explicit endpoint options.
capabilities.status: OpenAPI Wasm 0.2.0 is compatible by documented minimum
capabilities.caveat: 0.2.1 requires Wrappers ≥0.6.2, beyond observed 0.6.0. Current docs describe POST-for-read and retries; verify options against the pinned compatible binary.

capabilities.label: Analytics Buckets / Iceberg
capabilities.summary: Separate historical evidence analysis from transactional workloads, with explicit ingestion.
capabilities.caveat: Official creation docs say private alpha while the feature page says public alpha. Treat project eligibility and the lifecycle contract as unresolved.

capabilities.label: Iceberg SQL + catalog tools
capabilities.summary: Explore append-only analytical exports and catalog inspection.
capabilities.status: Current docs; compatibility with available Wrappers 0.6.0 unverified
capabilities.caveat: Iceberg FDW documents reads and INSERT, without UPDATE/DELETE/upsert. iceberg-js handles catalog metadata, not Parquet execution.

capabilities.label: Pipelines / Warehouse watch
capabilities.summary: Track managed CDC destinations and future warehouse work separately from the existing database.
capabilities.status: Pipelines public alpha; Warehouse under development
capabilities.caveat: Analytics Bucket replication is no longer supported. BigQuery is supported; ClickHouse, DuckLake, and Snowflake are Early Access. Project eligibility remains unverified.

capabilities.label: Vector Buckets
capabilities.summary: Evaluate alpha vector-object indexes for a separately scoped historical collection.
capabilities.status: Alpha; project and region access unverified
capabilities.caveat: Different API and storage from pgvector. Official batch limits disagree: 500 vs 1,000. Local buckets use pgvector while hosted buckets use S3 Vectors.

capabilities.label: AWS S3 Vectors wrapper
capabilities.summary: A third vector route: SQL access to an explicitly authorized AWS vector store.
capabilities.status: Optional wrapper; no AWS integration verified
capabilities.caveat: Separate from both Supabase Vector Buckets and local pgvector. Updates require delete/insert; configure AWS access and wrapper compatibility separately.

capabilities.label: Application Auth / OAuth
capabilities.summary: Explore explicit mapping between an application principal and its permitted operations.
capabilities.caveat: An Auth session does not establish an AgentTool signing identity, KINGDOM membership, or consent. Preserve current identity contracts.

capabilities.label: Participant-owned projects
capabilities.summary: Explore management OAuth and project claiming for participants who choose their own backend.
capabilities.status: Configuration unverified; this review created no connection
capabilities.caveat: Management OAuth differs from application OAuth. Ownership, billing, revocation, and export must be defined before provisioning.

capabilities.label: Developer MCP / skills / plugin
capabilities.summary: Operator tooling offers project scope, read-only mode, and narrower feature groups; skills provide workflow guidance.
capabilities.status: Researched only; no installation or connection
capabilities.caveat: Developer MCP is an operator capability, not a public KINGDOM agent contract. Omitted project scope can expose account-level tools.

capabilities.label: Database + object recovery
capabilities.summary: Rehearse database state, separately retained object bytes, keys, and receipt verification together.
capabilities.status: Backup metadata and restore exercise still unverified
capabilities.caveat: A database restore alone cannot resurrect deleted Storage objects. Ordinary object recovery and Iceberg snapshots have different contracts.

capabilities.label: Stripe Projects provisioning
capabilities.summary: Watch an optional developer provisioning integration for platforms.
capabilities.caveat: Provisioning projects does not process payments or change AgentTool’s marketplace, wallet, or settlement rules.

capabilities.label: Upstream discovery watch
capabilities.summary: Track grouped queues and opt-in Broadcast persistence as source-level research leads.
capabilities.status: PGMQ 1.12.0 and Realtime PR 2022; hosted rollout unverified
capabilities.caveat: These exceed the observed queue version or lack project rollout evidence. Do not design production correctness around them yet.

opportunities.title: 01 · Offline Commons workbench
opportunities.summary: Turn selected public metadata into a reproducible, provenance-bearing catalog that remains useful without an account or network.
opportunities.novelty: Use Supabase at build time while keeping the citizen-facing Commons accountless and offline. An FDW is optional; a bounded ordinary importer can implement the same projection.
opportunities.first_experiment: Start with 30 synthetic source records and one explicit local input file. Preserve upstream URL, licence observation, retrieval time, source version, digest, geography, and staleness policy in an ordinary table or file. Export twice; inspect locally with network disabled. Later test one approved provider against a method and byte budget.
success_criteria: Two exports from identical inputs have identical bytes and digest.
Every search result links to the exact source record and freshness information.
Offline browsing sends no queries or reading history to a provider.
Removing the original provider leaves the exported catalog readable.
stop_conditions: The adapter requires private user intent or undocumented access.
A SELECT emits an unexpected remote method, or a licence cannot support the intended copy.

opportunities.title: 02 · A finite Creation Loop queue
opportunities.summary: Commit one authorized turn’s receipt and queued intent together, then permit only a bounded worker effect.
opportunities.novelty: Transaction coupling can prevent a receipt claiming an intent that never reached the queue. Delivery state stays separate from permission and from the next voluntary turn.
opportunities.first_experiment: Use disposable PostgreSQL with pgmq 1.5.1, 100 synthetic intents, two consumers, and no external calls. Roll back after both receipt and enqueue statements, before their shared commit. Commit a visibility claim, terminate that consumer, and reconcile redelivery. Commit the deduplication marker and synthetic effect together; acknowledge the queue afterward.
success_criteria: Rollback leaves neither receipt nor message.
A committed claim expires after interruption; redelivery produces one application effect through an atomic deduplication/effect transaction.
Every job has a pre-existing explicit scope, resource bound, and stop condition.
REFLECT invitations remain inert until a separately chosen turn.
stop_conditions: Execution starts from an invitation or queue message alone.
Replay creates a duplicate effect or silently expands the work budget.

opportunities.title: 03 · A recoverable delivery ledger
opportunities.summary: Keep delivery intent in logged application state; use Cron and pg_net only to attempt transport and reconcile acknowledgments.
opportunities.novelty: Post-commit HTTP fits a transactional outbox, but pg_net’s private unlogged tables cannot serve as the durable ledger. Bind signed artifacts by exact digest across transport envelopes.
opportunities.first_experiment: Use an owned exact-version disposable cluster and an independently running loopback receiver, with at most 20 synthetic deliveries. Prove rollback emits no request. Commit logged intent, then perform an unclean restart of only that disposable cluster. Separately lose an acknowledgment after receiver success and reconcile with bounded retries.
success_criteria: Durable pending intent remains reconcilable after interruption.
The receiver commits the deduplication record and effect together, binds the key to the request digest, and rejects conflicting reuse.
Cron success and HTTP request ID cannot mark application delivery complete.
Original signed bytes verify independently of the JSON transport envelope.
stop_conditions: Correctness depends on private pg_net tables surviving a crash.
The worker logs secrets or retries an ambiguous economic effect.

opportunities.title: 04 · A library that preserves exact declarations
opportunities.summary: Search repository cards, authored declarations, dated observations, and withdrawals without conflating their meanings.
opportunities.novelty: Keep canonical artifacts by digest and JSONB as a rebuildable index. Provenance and verification status travel with each match; ranking never upgrades an assertion.
opportunities.first_experiment: Build a local fixture containing one valid card, one invalid schema, a structurally valid artifact with an invalid signature, altered canonical bytes, and a later withdrawal. Rebuild the index from exact source bytes; query the earlier and later revisions.
success_criteria: Each invalid input fails at its intended validation boundary.
The original byte digest survives index reconstruction.
Results show declaration vs observation and dated withdrawal separately.
No new field is added to kingdom.yaml to imply authority.
stop_conditions: JSONB output is treated as the original signed artifact.
Search rank, adopts declarations, or a source URL becomes a conformance badge.

opportunities.title: 05 · Return hints with durable reconciliation
opportunities.summary: A returning client receives minimal event hints, then resumes from authoritative correspondence history and its own cursor.
opportunities.novelty: Realtime improves responsiveness while complete history remains durable. A hosted metadata projection could later reuse the pure planner behind a separately reviewed executor.
opportunities.first_experiment: In an owned Realtime staging fixture, emit 30 synthetic private events from the database. Reconnect after interruption, combine bounded replay with cursor-based history, and test revocation on fresh and existing connections against a declared maximum window. Preserve the local projector’s loopback guard.
success_criteria: All 30 events reconcile without duplicate application effects.
Hints disclose only permitted IDs or digests.
Fresh subscriptions and authoritative history reads deny revoked access; existing-channel refresh or disconnect meets a declared, measured revocation window.
The client displays gaps or unavailable history explicitly.
stop_conditions: A replay buffer is treated as complete durable history or proof of presence.
The experiment changes the local projector into an unreviewed remote executor.

opportunities.title: 06 · An encrypted, portable evidence shelf
opportunities.summary: Carry selected ADDS ciphertext and a verification manifest across an object store and a separately retained offline export.
opportunities.novelty: A provider copy can support distribution while the portable encrypted bundle preserves an independent recovery path. Custody stays with the caller.
opportunities.first_experiment: Use a local S3 fixture and synthetic payloads with disposable keys. Upload encrypted objects, verify returned bytes, export an independent bundle, and restore with the original fixture unavailable.
success_criteria: Ciphertext integrity and authorized decryption are checked separately.
The manifest plus independently retained bytes restores every selected object.
The exercise distinguishes provider acknowledgment from verified restoration.
Keys remain outside provider-readable payloads and public evidence.
stop_conditions: The design depends on absent S3 Object Lock or database backups containing object bytes.
Revocation is described as erasing copies a recipient already holds.

opportunities.title: 07 · An evidence observatory
opportunities.summary: Compare dated operational receipts across releases using explicit analytical snapshots.
opportunities.novelty: Keep current operational decisions in the transactional store while an optional Iceberg projection supports historical comparison. Append is possible in current wrapper docs; the old managed replication route is retired.
opportunities.first_experiment: First export synthetic, privacy-minimized receipts to deterministic files and compare two releases. If an eligible disposable analytical service is later selected, test a pinned append-capable wrapper or explicit importer and verify snapshot-to-source digests.
success_criteria: The source revision and receipt digest survive export and analytical import.
Deleting the analytical projection does not change operational truth.
The chosen ingestion path works without Pipelines-to-Analytics replication.
stop_conditions: The required alpha access or compatible wrapper version is unavailable.
Metrics become participant rankings or analysis writes operational settlement state.

opportunities.title: 08 · Release and recovery rehearsal
opportunities.summary: Exercise migrations, permissions, objects, and freshness with synthetic records before a production change.
opportunities.novelty: Combine role-negative checks, independent object restoration, and simulated replica lag in one bounded evidence packet for the deployment owner.
opportunities.first_experiment: Start locally: seed synthetic rows and encrypted objects, apply the proposed migration using the existing migration mechanism, restore both data planes, and simulate a stale public projection. Any later managed branch has a separate explicit scope.
success_criteria: Unauthorized role reads fail while approved application reads succeed.
Both database rows and selected object bytes restore and verify.
Stale public reads show their revision; revocation-sensitive reads use the primary.
The existing canonical release and migration path retains ownership.
stop_conditions: A branch merge initiates a second production migration writer.
A regional replica is treated as proof of global service readiness.

opportunities.title: 09 · An optional participant-owned backend
opportunities.summary: Explore a KINGDOM participant choosing their own Supabase project, while AgentTool offers a narrow application contract.
opportunities.novelty: Project ownership can be separated from application interoperability. Management tools remain operator-only; a participant can export artifacts without adopting the provider as authority.
opportunities.first_experiment: Create an offline ownership and revocation contract using two fictional participants, with explicit organization owner, billing owner, application role, export format, and disconnect behavior. Use mocks only; provision nothing.
success_criteria: Management OAuth and application OAuth have separate audiences and scopes.
Participant A cannot select participant B’s resources in mocked negative cases.
Disconnect and export behavior are explicit and testable.
Public agent tools expose finite application operations rather than project administration.
stop_conditions: The design requires an account-wide token in an agent-facing client.
Provider identity silently replaces an AgentTool signing identity or KINGDOM declaration.

findings.title: The seven layers are real; these connections are our interpretation
findings.detail: KINGDOM declares soul, runtime, nervous, fleet, economy, commerce, and os. AgentTool’s observed card says infra/nervous. A line on this map proposes a useful fit; it does not change membership, validate practice, or grant execution authority.

findings.title: Available does not mean installed
findings.detail: The 2026-09-05 catalog found pgmq 1.5.1, pg_jsonschema 0.3.3, and Wrappers 0.6.0 available but absent. This map did not rerun the database inventory. Matching upstream source tags still do not prove hosted package parity.

findings.title: A transport buffer is not a delivery ledger
findings.detail: In pg_net v0.20.0, request and response tables are private and unlogged. Build correctness on logged application intent and explicit receiver acknowledgment; keep signed source bytes independent of JSONB encoding.

findings.title: SQL can conceal remote calls
findings.detail: The current OpenAPI documentation allows POST-for-read and retries. Its 0.2.1 Wasm requires a newer Wrappers version than the observed available 0.6.0; investigate compatible 0.2.0 separately.

findings.title: The analytics story changed
findings.detail: Pipelines no longer replicates into Analytics Buckets. Bucket documentation also disagrees about private vs public alpha. The map therefore treats analytics access and ingestion as experiments.

findings.title: Vector docs need an API-level check
findings.detail: The creation guide gives a 500-vector batch maximum while the limits page says 1,000. Keep any prototype at 500 or fewer until the selected API confirms its contract. Local pgvector behavior does not establish hosted S3 Vectors performance.

findings.title: A queue cannot create the next turn
findings.detail: Creation Loop stages run from SENSE through REFLECT. A child invitation requires a separate deliberate start; queue receipt, schedule, or readiness assessment cannot supply that choice or execution permission.

findings.title: Similar names carry different contracts
findings.detail: The live /public/kingdom/framework response is a project card. thekingdom.dev/kingdom.json is an authored map/measurement overlay, not the AgentTool registry schema. /public/kingdom remains the doctrine library.

findings.title: Framework inspection has a boundary
findings.detail: The inspected KINGDOM OS checkout supplies web-facing schemas and roadmap material. The canonical local registry/runtime checkout was absent at its documented paths, so no core scheduler or live fleet behavior is claimed.

findings.title: Promising upstream work is not a hidden supported API
findings.detail: PGMQ 1.12.0 grouped queues and Realtime PR 2022’s opt-in persistence are public source leads. Their rollout and project compatibility are unverified; they are not prerequisites for the first pilots.
